comments.author: participant1
comments.body:
Reproduction of test_map_meta failure with pandas 3.0

I was able to reproduce the failure locally in test_map_meta when testing against pandas 3.0.

**Environment**
Python 3.12.3
pytest 9.0.2
pandas 3.0
local checkout of main

**Command used**
```
PYTEST_DISABLE_PLUGIN_AUTOLOAD=1 \
pytest -o addopts= \
dask/dataframe/dask_expr/tests/test_collection.py::test_map_meta -s
```

**Debugging details**
To understand the failure, I added debug prints just before the first assertion in test_map_meta:

```
print(f"DEBUG - RESULT META INDEX: {result._meta.index}")
print(f"DEBUG - EXPECTED INDEX: {expected.index}")

```
**Observed output**
```
DEBUG - RESULT META INDEX: RangeIndex(start=0, stop=0, step=1)
DEBUG - EXPECTED INDEX: RangeIndex(start=0, stop=100, step=1)
```


The test then fails at:
assert result._meta.index.equals(expected.index)

Interpretation
This indicates that when calling:
`df.x.map(lambda x: x + 1, meta=expected.iloc[:0])`

the resulting _meta does not preserve the index information from the provided meta. Instead, _meta.index is inferred as an empty RangeIndex(0, 0), even though the supplied meta carries the full index type.

This reproduces the CI failure and suggests that index handling during _meta inference for Series.map has changed (or regressed) with pandas 3.0.

comments.author: reporter
comments.body:
> [@participant3](https://github.com/participant3) https://github.com/dask/dask/actions/runs/21276378399/job/61236740674
> 
> Briefly looking at the test, I see a random.choice in it, which would explain why the warning only appears occasionally.

Looking at it closer, I'm reading

```
dask/dataframe/io/parquet/arrow.py:603: in read_partition
    pd.Categorical(
_ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ 

values = array([2], dtype=int32)
categories = Index([1, 2, 3, 4], dtype='int32')
[...]
E           pandas.errors.Pandas4Warning: Constructing a Categorical with a dtype and values containing non-null entries not in that dtype's categories is deprecated and will raise in a future version.
```

which makes no sense.
I can trigger the warning with
```python
pd.Categorical(values = np.array([5], dtype=np.int32), categories = pd.Index([1, 2, 3, 4], dtype='int32')
```

To me it smells of a race condition within pandas where different dask threads have different values and categories in their stacks and they call `categories.get_indexer_for(values)` in parallel, but they may share a common global state and thus interfere with each other. It reminds me of https://github.com/pydata/xarray/issues/10923.

However, just like the other issue I just linked, I'm utterly failing to reproduce it locally - either synthetically or with the dask test suite.

comments.author: reporter
comments.body:
I've tested https://github.com/pandas-dev/pandas/pull/63783 vs. pandas git tip on 3.14 and 3.14t (https://github.com/dask/dask/pull/12284).

TL;DR; the pandas PR seems to make all flakiness disappear, and I consider it a blocker to 3.14t support for dask.dataframe.


## Shared based environments
```
=== 3.14 ===
mamba env create -n dask-314 -f continuous_integration/environment-3.14.yaml 
conda activate dask-314
mamba install pytest-repeat
pip install . git+https://github.com/dask/distributed

=== 3.14t ===
wget https://raw.githubusercontent.com/reporter/dask/refs/heads/314t_pandas/continuous_integration/environment-3.14t.yaml
mamba env create -n dask-314t -f environment-3.14t.yaml
conda activate dask-314t
conda uninstall -y -v --force msgpack-python
MSGPACK_PUREPYTHON=1 pip install msgpack --no-binary msgpack --no-cache --force-reinstall -v
mamba install pytest-repeat
pip install . git+https://github.com/dask/distributed
```

## pandas variants
- pandas 3.0.0
`mamba install pandas=3.0.0 --force-reinstall`
- pandas git tip
`pip install git+https://github.com/pandas-dev/pandas.git@2455fb9066628929be67011d01bb62a098cdb9ea`
- https://github.com/pandas-dev/pandas/pull/63783
`pip install git+https://github.com/reporter/pandas.git@727c73034f9d2c63d7e0164a10c2f5e367b017c6`

## Test run
These are tests that are frequently seen to fail in our CI throughout all Python versions:
```
taskset -c 0,1,2,3 python -m pytest --pyargs --count=100 \
    dask/dataframe/io/tests/test_parquet.py::test_filter_nonpartition_columns \
    dask/dataframe/io/tests/test_parquet.py::test_roundtrip_partitioned_pyarrow_dataset \
    dask/dataframe/io/tests/test_parquet.py::test_arrow_partitioning
```
# Outcome
- Python 3.14, Pandas 3.0.0: I failed to replicate CI failures locally (probably due to much faster hardware than CI)
- Python 3.14t, Pandas 3.0.0: 3~15% failure rate on the above tests
- Python 3.14t, Pandas main git tip: same as 3.0.0
- Python 3.14t, https://github.com/pandas-dev/pandas/pull/63783: all failures disappear. :<nick>: 

Because I failed to replicate the failures on the GIL-enabled interpreter, I cannot assertively say if these race conditions are a regression in Pandas 3.0 or if they were already there in 2.3. I can only observe from git blame that `Index._ensure_mapping_populated` has not been touched in at least 3 years.
